To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the electrocatalytic reduction of nitrate ions on tin-modified platinum (Sn/Pt) and palladium-deposed gold (Sn/Pd/Au), electrodes is a two-step process.

the tin-modified platinum electrode exhibits an enhanced electrocatalytic effect on the reduction of nitrite ions, while the tin-modified palladium electrode is more efficient in the electrochemical reduction of nitrate ions.

the Sn/Pt and Sn/Au electrodes have shown a higher electrocatabolism of nitrate ions than any electrode so-far reported in the literature, and the Sn/Pd/Aug electrode has shown an electrocatalytic reduction of nitrate ions with a high selectivity for nitrogen gas.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the electrochemical reduction of nitrate ions in aqueous acidic media on Sn-modified electrodes.
the electrochemical reduction of nitrate ions at the Sn/Pt electrode in alkaline solution.
the electrochemical reduction of nitrate ions on Sn/Pt and Sn/Au/Pd electrodes, and the effects of the electrode materials and the reaction conditions on the reduction products.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the electrochemical reduction of nitrate ions on the tin-modified platinum electrode is a four-electron process, and that on the tin-modifed palladium-deposiited gold electrode, a two-electron process is predominant.
tin modification of Pt and Pd/Au electrodes enhances the electrocatalytic reduction of nitrate ions.
the Sn/Pd/AU electrode has a higher catalytic efficiency than the Sn/Pt electrode, which in turn is more efficient than any other electrode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the electrochemical reduction of nitrate ions on Sn/Pt and Sn/Au is a two-step process.
Sn/Pt was a better electrocatalyst for the reduction of NO3- to NH4+ than the Sn/Pd/AU electrode.
the electrochemical reduction of nitrate on tin-modified platinum electrodes is a two-electron process, while that on tin-modified palladium electrodes is a four-electron process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tin-modified platinum is a highly efficient electrocatalyst for nitrate reduction.

the Sn/Pt and Sn/ Pd/Au electrode surfaces can be used as efficient catalysts for the electrocatalytic reduction of nitrate to ammonium ions, and the Sn/Pd/Aug electrode can be used as an efficient catalyst for the electrocata-lytic reduction of nitrate ions to N2O or N2.
Sn/Pt and Sn/Au are the most active electrocatalysts for the reduction of NO3−.
